You're building a new feature for Nxeon, a VPS/hosting platform. Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Prisma/Postgres. Production repo: /opt/nxeon (git, branch `main`), staging mirror at /opt/nxeon-staging (own `.env`, own systemd service `nxeon-staging-web.service` on port 8080 locally, real public domain `staging.nxeon.cloud`).

## Goal

Build a Google Search Console integration that finds real SEO "striking distance" opportunities — queries where nxeon.cloud already gets meaningful impressions but ranks outside the top 10, meaning there's demonstrated interest but no page winning it yet. Read-only against Google's API; only ever writes to Nxeon's own DB. This mirrors the philosophy of the existing `worker/marketing.ts` discovery sweep (`lib/marketing/discovery.ts`, models `MarketingSource`/`MarketingSignal`/`MarketingDraft`, admin review page `/admin/marketing`) — read public/authorized data, surface findings, a human reviews and acts — but it's a distinct system (SEO content-gap discovery vs. social-listening), so it gets its own tables, not reuse of the marketing models. Look at that existing sweep for the established conventions (kill-switch Setting via `getSettingBool`, how sweeps are registered/paced in `worker/index.ts`, the admin review page pattern) and follow them for consistency.

## Credentials already provisioned — do not create new ones

`/etc/nxeon/google-search-console.env` (600, root-only) already contains:
```
GSC_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=...
GSC_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=...
GSC_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI=https://nxeon.cloud/api/admin/integrations/google-search-console/callback
```
The OAuth client is created, published (non-sensitive scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters.readonly`, no verification review needed), and the Search Console API is enabled for the GCP project. A second redirect URI, `https://staging.nxeon.cloud/api/admin/integrations/google-search-console/callback`, is being added to the same OAuth client by the owner so you can safely test the full live flow on staging before production ever sees it.

Read these into the app the same way other `/etc/nxeon/*.env` files are wired in elsewhere in this codebase (check how `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN_TRYNXEON` or similar get loaded — likely sourced into the systemd unit's environment, or read via `dotenv`-style loading at process start; follow whatever the existing pattern is, don't invent a new loading mechanism). Staging needs its OWN `GSC_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI` value (the staging URL above) in `/opt/nxeon-staging/.env` — production's `.env`/env-loading keeps the `nxeon.cloud` one. Don't hardcode either URI in code; both come from env.

## What to build

1. **Prisma schema** — two new tables:
   - A small integration-state table holding the encrypted OAuth refresh token, the connected Google account's email, and connection timestamp. Encrypt the refresh token with the existing `lib/crypto-box.ts` (`encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret`) — same pattern already used for `Inbox.smtpPassEnc`/`imapPassEnc`. This is a singleton in practice (one connection for the whole platform) — model it however fits Prisma idiom here (a table with at most one row, or a dedicated `Setting`-style key — check how `Setting` (`lib/settings.ts`) is used elsewhere for single-value platform state and decide whether this warrants its own table or fits that pattern; a refresh token is a secret so it likely wants its own table with proper encryption rather than living in the general `Setting` table, but use your judgement).
   - `SeoOpportunity`: id, query (string), page (string, nullable — the currently-ranking URL if GSC reports one), impressions (int), clicks (int), ctr (float), position (float), status (enum: NEW / REVIEWED / ACTIONED / DISMISSED, default NEW), firstSeenAt, lastSeenAt, createdAt/updatedAt. Unique on query (or query+page if a query can legitimately have multiple ranking pages — check real GSC response shape once you have a live connection and decide). Upsert semantics: re-running the sweep updates impressions/clicks/position/lastSeenAt on existing rows rather than duplicating.

   Check how schema changes actually get applied in this codebase (look at `prisma/migrations/` for the established workflow — `prisma migrate dev`/`deploy`, or a different convention) and follow it. **Generate the migration but do NOT apply it to the live production database** — that's an explicit stop-condition below.

2. **`lib/seo/searchConsole.ts`** — no `googleapis` npm package (not installed, don't add it for one API surface). Use plain `fetch`:
   - Build the Google OAuth consent URL (`response_type=code`, the stored client id + redirect uri, `scope=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters.readonly`, `access_type=offline`, `prompt=consent` — the last two are required to actually get a refresh token back, not just an access token).
   - Exchange an authorization code for tokens (`POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`).
   - Refresh an access token from the stored refresh token (same endpoint, `grant_type=refresh_token`).
   - Call the Search Console `searchanalytics.query` REST endpoint (`POST https://www.googleapis.com/webmasters/v3/sites/{siteUrl}/searchAnalytics/query`) grouped by query+page, for a reasonable lookback window (90 days is a sane default — make it configurable). **Important**: once you have a live connection, check whether nxeon.cloud is verified in Search Console as a domain property (`sc-domain:nxeon.cloud`) or a URL-prefix property (`https://nxeon.cloud/`) — the `siteUrl` path segment must be URL-encoded exactly right for whichever it is, and calling `sites.list` on the API first is the reliable way to find the exact verified property string rather than guessing.

3. **API routes**:
   - `GET /api/admin/integrations/google-search-console/connect` — admin-auth-gated (match whatever auth-checking convention other `/admin` API routes in this codebase use), redirects (302) to the Google consent URL.
   - `GET /api/admin/integrations/google-search-console/callback` — exchanges the code, encrypts + stores the refresh token + connected account email, redirects back to the admin UI with a success/error indicator in the query string.

4. **Admin UI** — check `lib/admin-groups.ts`'s `marketing` group (it already has entries for `marketing`, `studio`, and six `coldemail-*` entries) and add a new entry there, e.g. `{ key: "seo", label: "SEO", icon: "chart", tabs: [{ label: "Opportunities", href: "/admin/seo" }, { label: "Settings", href: "/admin/seo/settings" }] }` — match the existing `AdminEntry`/`AdminGroup` shape exactly (read a few neighboring entries first). Build:
   - A settings/status view: connection status (not connected → "Connect Google Search Console" button hitting the `/connect` route; connected → "Connected as {email}, last synced {time}" plus a disconnect action), and the volume/position thresholds as tunable Settings (`getSettingInt`/equivalent, following the `marketingDiscoverySweep` pattern of a tunable threshold Setting with a sane default).
   - An opportunities list/table: query, page, impressions, clicks, position, status — filterable by status, with server actions (follow the `lib/actions-*.ts` convention already used elsewhere, e.g. `lib/actions-coldemail.ts`) to mark a row REVIEWED/ACTIONED/DISMISSED.

5. **Worker sweep** — `worker/seo.ts` exporting `seoOpportunitySweep()`, thin wrapper calling into `lib/seo/` logic (mirror how `worker/marketing.ts` is a thin wrapper over `lib/marketing/discovery.ts`). Behind a kill-switch Setting (default however you judge fits — check what other read-only, low-risk sweeps default to). Weekly cadence — check how `worker/index.ts`'s loop paces sweeps at different intervals (some run every 2 min, some 15 min) and find/follow the existing mechanism for a much longer interval like weekly, rather than inventing a new scheduling primitive. Sweep logic: refresh the token, pull the last ~90 days of query+page data, filter to real volume (above the tunable threshold) and position outside the top 10 (roughly 11–30 is the realistic "content gap, worth a look" zone — don't over-engineer a "does a good page already exist" NLP classifier, that's a human judgment call in v1; just surface the raw list well), upsert into `SeoOpportunity`.

## Ground rules

- Isolate yourself: `cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-gsc -b feature/gsc-seo-opportunities`, symlink `node_modules`/`.env`, work only there. Never build in the live `/opt/nxeon` tree.
- This reads Google's API and writes only to Nxeon's own DB — never anything that could look like automated posting/scraping of a third party beyond the authorized Search Console API itself.
- Run `npm run build` and `npx tsc --noEmit` clean in the worktree.
- **Stop condition — do NOT touch the production database or deploy anywhere.** Generate the Prisma migration file but do not run it against the live production DB. Do not merge to main, do not touch staging or production services. This involves a real external OAuth integration and a schema change — both want a human look before going live, unlike the smaller app-logic fixes from earlier sessions. Commit everything on `feature/gsc-seo-opportunities` and stop.
- If you get far enough to actually complete a live OAuth handshake, note in your report whether you were able to (you likely can't fully complete it from an isolated worktree dev server, since the redirect URI is fixed to a real public domain — that's expected and fine; the real first live test happens after this deploys to staging).

Report back: what you built (files touched/created), the migration file's contents (so it can be reviewed before anyone runs it), the commit hash, and exactly what manual steps remain before this can go live on staging (e.g. "add the staging env var, deploy, click Connect, verify a real sync").

+/// A dedicated table (not the general `Setting` store) because a refresh token

+model GscConnection {
+  id              String    @id @default(cuid())
+  refreshTokenEnc String // encryptSecret(...) — never plaintext
+  accountEmail    String // the connected Google account, shown in the admin UI
+  // The exact verified Search Console property string returned by sites.list,

## Summary

Built the full GSC SEO Opportunity Discovery feature on branch `feature/gsc-seo-opportunities` in an isolated worktree at `/opt/nxeon-wt-gsc` (with its own independent `node_modules` — see note below). Two commits, both build clean (`npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` pass with exit 0).

**Files created:**
- `prisma/schema.prisma` — `GscConnection` (singleton, `refreshTokenEnc` via `lib/crypto-box`) + `SeoOpportunity` (unique on `[query, page]`) + `SeoOpportunityStatus` enum
- `prisma/gsc-seo-opportunities.sql` — the reviewable migration SQL (see below), **not applied anywhere**
- `lib/seo/searchConsole.ts` — OAuth consent/exchange/refresh via plain `fetch`, `sites.list`/`searchAnalytics.query`, and the `GscConnection` DB accessor (modeled on `lib/cloudflare-oauth.ts`)
- `lib/seo/opportunities.ts` — pure filter logic (impressions ≥ threshold, position 11–30)
- `worker/seo.ts` — `seoOpportunitySweep()`, wired into `worker/index.ts` on a weekly (`7*24h`) tick, kill-switched by `seo_monitor_enabled` (default true)
- `app/api/admin/integrations/google-search-console/{connect,callback}/route.ts` — admin-gated (`realUser` + `canAccess(role,"platform")`), CSRF state cookie
- `lib/actions-seo.ts`, `app/admin/seo/page.tsx`, `app/admin/seo/settings/page.tsx`, `components/admin/seo/*.tsx` — opportunity list with status filter/actions, connection card, threshold settings, "Sync now"
- `lib/admin-groups.ts` / `lib/rbac.ts` — new "SEO" nav entry under Marketing, gated to `platform` area

**One mistake caught and fixed along the way:** the first `npx prisma generate` ran against the shared `node_modules` symlink and briefly overwrote *production's* generated `@prisma/client`. I restored prod's client immediately (`cd /opt/nxeon && npx prisma generate` against its own unmodified schema — verified clean, confirmed no `SeoOpportunity` type leaked into prod's `node_modules`) and then gave the worktree its own real `node_modules` via `npm ci` so it can never happen again. Separately, an `npx prisma format` call reflowed ~160 unrelated lines across other models — caught before it mattered and fixed in a second commit so the diff against `main` is now a clean, purely-additive 1,454-line diff across 15 files (only `lib/rbac.ts` is a 2-line addition to an existing file otherwise).

